CodeElement: Walkable surface and physical observation coordinates
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Legacy locate requires a cell center within numeric tolerance. Continuous motion uses a tile only as an index and checks the traversed tiles, including corner and border coverage.
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Not applicable to grid coordinates or swept clearance
SupportedBiologicalClaim: The audited coordinates and passability are software state.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A walkable tile does not imply that a worker knows the tile or its geometry. Surface resolution, cubic clearance and corner logic represent the world motor.

CodeElement: Local food and step cue extraction
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Enumerate up to four legal cardinal steps. Bounded breadth-first search returns nonempty food cues with graph distance and first direction. Continuous mode checks a clear segment from each sampled point to its indexed food.
EvidenceLocators: B2-F04 pp. 76–78, §§3.1–3.2, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B2-F10 pp. 358–361, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Feeding events per contact and arena worker flows
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Food contact and post-contact acceptance can be distinguished experimentally. Exploration can expose resources and depends on encounter context.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Graph BFS can expose nonempty food around a corner without the body visiting those cells. It supplies exact identity and first edge with no sensor, no miss and no time-to-detection.

CodeElement: Colony-specific scalar trail cue
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Read only the actor's colony field for each legal neighboring cell. Continuous motion provides previous-step direction from the last heading when a previous route position exists.
InformationChannel: Shared scalar field with exact colony filter
EvidenceLocators: B2-P10 p. 796, species-specific and stereochemical tests, Scheme 1 and Fig. 1, Tables 1–2 | B2-P15 pp. 753–756, Results, Eq. 1–5, Fig. 1, Tables I–II | B2-P16 pp. 1618–1622, Results and model fit, Figs. 2, 4 and 6, Table 1 and Online Appendix B Tables B1–B3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: GC–MS and EAG, cross-colony aged-branch choices, fitted Y-arm detection
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Workers respond to rectal-sac chemistry. A marked paper segment is effective for workers from a different L. niger colony in P15.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Exact ColonyId masking would erase an otherwise present foreign cue. A single adjacent-tile field value does not express substrate dose, chemical identity, antenna sampling or polarity.

CodeElement: Explicit vision, mechanosensory and environmental sensors
CurrentRuleOrGuard: There is no receptor, image, light, vibrational or multimodal noisy perception path. Contact, distance and clearance are direct software predicates.
InformationChannel: Missing multimodal input and separate software scheduling
EvidenceLocators: B2-F02 pp. 289–296, rotation and light interventions, Figs. 12–14, Tables II–IV | B2-F03 PDF pp. 6–10, Results, Figs. 1–4 and S1.1–S1.12, Tables S1.1–S1.3 | B2-F09 pp. 538–540, §§3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–3 | B2-P07 pp. 264–266, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–5 | B2-P12 Accepted manuscript pp. 12–16, Experiments 1 and 0, Figs. 1, 2 and 4
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Track shape under changed light, substrate speed, room effect, controlled contact-to-fork direction null
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Light and visual context affect some navigation assays. Texture affected locomotion. Contact did not reveal next-fork direction in the controlled P12 test.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: There is no visual or other receptor model here. Peer or brood contact elsewhere in Core does not feed this foraging decision. The paper outcomes do not imply global resource coordinates.

CodeElement: Foraging enrollment and ownership
CurrentRuleOrGuard: First activation requires an unloaded worker with capacity at its own exact depot. Initialize home path and heading or require prior trace continuity on reactivation.
EvidenceLocators: B2-F10 pp. 358–361, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–3 | B2-P08 pp. 62–68, Results, Figs. 1–5, Tables 1–2 | B2-P09 pp. 562–566, Results and discussion, Fig. 1, Tables 1–3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Worker departure flow and post-scout exit in a defined window
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Spontaneous exploratory departures and departure following recruitment occur under different experimental conditions.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The host or physiology selects the task. Exact depot, eligibility, initial heading and event start do not encode the measured effect of scout return, deprivation and local cues.

CodeElement: Decision priority and bounded return
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Priority is loaded home delivery, then away-from-home return when loaded, already returning or at path/move bound, then local food, then valid learned next edge, then weighted search.
EvidenceLocators: B2-F02 pp. 289–296, rotation and light interventions, Figs. 12–14, Tables II–IV | B2-F05 pp. 503–504, §3.1, Fig. 1, Tables 1–2 | B2-P07 pp. 264–266, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Reorientation under visual manipulations and uptake at a second source while returning
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Workers can orient towards a nest after a trip, and can drink on a homeward leg even after an earlier intake.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A loaded worker away from home reverses the trace before considering other food cues. Exact reverse steps, hard trip cutoffs and blocked-leg Rest are unmeasured.

CodeElement: Nearest local resource and unbiased distance ties
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Minimize graph cell distance, sort equal-distance cues by physical cell and draw uniformly. When not in the source cell approach via its first edge.
InformationChannel: Graph-distance ranking of exact local food cues
EvidenceLocators: B2-F04 pp. 76–78, §§3.1–3.2, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B2-F08 pp. 117–121, Results and interpretation, Figs. 1–4, Table 1 | B2-P11 pp. 191–194, Results, Figs. 1–3 and A1 | B2-P15 pp. 753–756, Results, Eq. 1–5, Fig. 1, Tables I–II
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Post-contact acceptance, food-type return and same-distance colony occupancy
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Food chemistry and route geometry can change decisions under controlled conditions. Equidistant feeders can receive unequal visitation.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The published colony comparisons do not isolate an individual with simultaneous cue access. No general distance-only ranking or uniform tie law was measured. Code ties remove identifier bias.

CodeElement: Weighted exploration and direction persistence
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Exclude the predecessor when alternatives exist except a one-signal correction. Give visited cells base 1 and other cells explore_weight, add persistence for current heading, and add the optional normalized trail term before a deterministic weighted draw.
EvidenceLocators: B2-F01 PDF pp. 3–6, Effect of inclination and extended walker analysis, Figs. 1–5, Table 1 | B2-F03 PDF pp. 6–10, Results, Figs. 1–4 and S1.1–S1.12, Tables S1.1–S1.3 | B2-F10 pp. 358–361, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–3 | B2-P01 pp. 772–774, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–3 | B2-P13 p. 679, Results, Fig. 1
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Turning and segment length, trial flow, bifurcation choice and repeated trail choice
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Movement has directional structure. Preferred branching can depend on angle, start-relative bearing and illumination. Stable trail-ignoring specialists were not detected in P13.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A constant straight bonus, loop-erased visited-cell penalty and predecessor mask are not a fitted angular kernel. F03 reuses F01 tracks and also has a separate new light assay.

CodeElement: Experienced route acquisition, reversal and expiry
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Tile moves append or truncate at an already visited cell. Successful collection records the current path and timestamp as one learned route. Return traces the current path backward. Memory reuses only the next legal step at a recognized cell.
InformationChannel: One individual path trace and remembered route
EvidenceLocators: B2-F06 pp. 144–146, Results, experiments 1–5, Figs. 1–4 | B2-F07 pp. 190–193, Results, Figs. 1–4 and 6, Appendix Tables A1–A2 pp. 195–196 | B2-P02 pp. 521–523, §3 and Fig. 2, Figs. 1–2 | B2-P03 Results, Decision making and Pheromone deposition, Figs. 1–3, S1 Table | B2-P07 pp. 264–266, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Choice accuracy across visits, route-cue conflict, after-training test and room shift
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Private route knowledge and visual context affect foraging routes. Learnability and prior exposure matter and errors remain after experience.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A single successful pickup writes a perfect stored trace for its available legal successors. There is no visit-dependent accuracy, graded memory cue conflict or general measured expiry.

CodeElement: Food uptake and load eligibility
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Reject out of reach, depleted, full or loaded-clearance failure. Amount is minimum of request, source and remaining capacity. Move the source's current constituent proportions to external cargo.
EvidenceLocators: B2-F04 pp. 76–78, §§3.1–3.2, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B2-F05 pp. 503–504, §3.1, Fig. 1, Tables 1–2 | B2-F08 pp. 117–121, Results and interpretation, Figs. 1–4, Table 1
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Post-contact intake, timed drinking and returned liquid volume
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Workers may ingest different quantities depending on food and prior intake. Both drinking and refraining after contact occur.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Integer conservation and clearance are software guarantees. Actual crop filling, drinking duration and taste do not map to one fixed-time external cargo commit.

CodeElement: Delivery to actual depot and empty return
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Deliver only at reachable nest contact and, for legacy surface, matching cell. Move all food cargo into colony nest stock. A remembered home tile in a mixed world may initiate traversal to the depot for an empty return.
InformationChannel: Physical depot delivery and shared stock accounting
EvidenceLocators: B2-F05 pp. 503–504, §3.1, Fig. 1, Tables 1–2 | B2-P09 pp. 562–566, Results and discussion, Fig. 1, Tables 1–3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Returning scouts, within-nest unloading and trophallactic observations
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Returning workers bring food and can transfer it through contacts in the nest.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A single depot receives the entire external load. Empty connector return is a route event, not evidence for resource transfer or recruitment.

CodeElement: Movement geometry, speed and execution failure
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Require clear swept segment and elapsed-time speed limit. Legacy planar resolution also requires adjacent located cells. Continuous foraging move clock uses maximum of configured step/connector time and a rounded travel-time lower bound.
InformationChannel: Scheduled translation and swept world geometry
EvidenceLocators: B2-F01 PDF pp. 3–6, Effect of inclination and extended walker analysis, Figs. 1–5, Table 1 | B2-F09 pp. 538–540, §§3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–3 | B2-P02 pp. 521–523, §3 and Fig. 2, Figs. 1–2 | B2-P04 PDF pp. 4–6, Results, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Observed free-walking path speeds on measured substrates and with route cues
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Travel rates and track shape can differ with substrate, incline and experience. A local trail does not always raise walking speed.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The default global speed ceiling is lower than mean path speeds in selected unloaded worker assays. It is shared across motion contexts, with no load-specific measurement or turning law.

CodeElement: Discovered surface-to-depot connector
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Search quantized passable neighbor edges toward a surface plane offset by loaded half-extent. Require an open neighboring surface tile with clear access. Cache one path per ant and walk it one waypoint at a time.
InformationChannel: Bounded geometry planner and individual cached connector
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No matched subterranean portal-choice experiment reviewed
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Geometric feasibility and saved waypoint traversal are engineering operations.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A height-biased search sees quantized geometry ahead within its budget. That is not measured knowledge of passages, a visual beacon or an experimentally established path integrator. Persistent blockage does not elicit replanning.

CodeElement: Foraging wake, suspension and terminal ownership
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Reschedule after a completed or rejected owned action. Increment failure counters for rejection. Stop removes outstanding owned events and disables the forager while preserving its record.
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Not applicable to cancellation and replay ordering
SupportedBiologicalClaim: The wake owner and action token are software constructs.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Repeated rejection, timed idle and queue cancellation do not measure abandonment, rest, persistence or response latency.

CodeElement: Loaded move deposition rule
CurrentRuleOrGuard: If the actor carried food before the movement, deposit a fixed increment to the destination cell capped at trail_cap_units. Connector moves and within-tile approaches are separate branches and do not deposit through this branch.
InformationChannel: Synthetic field increment from committed loaded motion
EvidenceLocators: B2-F05 pp. 503–504, §3.1, Fig. 1, Tables 1–2 | B2-F08 pp. 117–121, Results and interpretation, Figs. 1–4, Table 1 | B2-P05 PDF pp. 4–6, §§3.1–3.3, Figs. 2–3 | B2-P06 pp. 371–373, Results, Figs. 1–3, Table 1 | B2-P08 pp. 62–68, Results, Figs. 1–5, Tables 1–2 | B2-P09 pp. 562–566, Results and discussion, Fig. 1, Tables 1–3 | B2-P10 p. 796, species-specific and stereochemical tests, Scheme 1 and Fig. 1, Tables 1–2 | B2-P15 pp. 753–756, Results, Eq. 1–5, Fig. 1, Tables I–II
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Observed marks by trip and food, traffic and relay, and synthetic compound bioassay
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Foragers mark substrate. Marking varies with direction, food, prior mark, position and encounters. Both outbound marks and food-recipient relay have been observed.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The rule counts loaded cross-tile arrivals with a fixed increment and cap. No outbound marking, context-dependent secretion, food recipient relay or measured dose is implemented.

CodeElement: Decay, cutoff and sparse trail maintenance
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Apply exponential decay on read/write and periodic maintenance. Clamp effective concentration to zero below cutoff. Periodic environment events erase zero entries and update the rest.
InformationChannel: Independent tile decay and numerical cutoff
EvidenceLocators: B2-P07 pp. 264–266, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–5 | B2-P08 pp. 62–68, Results, Figs. 1–5, Tables 1–2 | B2-P15 pp. 753–756, Results, Eq. 1–5, Fig. 1, Tables I–II
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Fitted choice aging time constant and 15 cm completion relative to baseline
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Some behavioral response weakens with time. P15 fits an assumed exponential law to a specific aged-bridge assay. P07 shows persistence depends on cue history and context.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: No chemical mass measurement, diffusion or advection exists in Core. The time constant, threshold-crossing duration and raw chemical half-life are distinct.

CodeElement: Trail influence, bounded correction and private memory precedence
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Only one visible signal on the predecessor can permit immediate reversal. Add trail_weight times capped normalized signal to the exploration and persistence weights. A chosen edge with signal above cutoff is labeled FollowTrail.
InformationChannel: Local scalar response after private-route priority
EvidenceLocators: B2-F06 pp. 144–146, Results, experiments 1–5, Figs. 1–4 | B2-F07 pp. 190–193, Results, Figs. 1–4 and 6, Appendix Tables A1–A2 pp. 195–196 | B2-P01 pp. 772–774, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–3 | B2-P02 pp. 521–523, §3 and Fig. 2, Figs. 1–2 | B2-P03 Results, Decision making and Pheromone deposition, Figs. 1–3, S1 Table | B2-P04 PDF pp. 4–6, Results, Figs. 1–5 | B2-P13 p. 679, Results, Fig. 1 | B2-P16 pp. 1618–1622, Results and model fit, Figs. 2, 4 and 6, Table 1 and Online Appendix B Tables B1–B3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Cue-gap reversals, fork choice, strip occupancy, post-training accuracy and fitted extract response
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Local chemical cues affect some choices and corrections. Dose response, geometry and experience have distinct or interacting effects. Several proposed effects were not significant or failed replication.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The sole-predecessor exception, clipped additive weight and deterministic memory precedence are not equivalent to those assays. FollowTrail is a visible-cue label on the chosen edge, including the zero-response configuration.

CodeElement: Colony recruitment as emergent outcome
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Workers can change their steps through the shared field. Departure uses the individual enrollment/autonomy policy. There is no separate recruit state, scout announcement, antennal recruitment exchange or direct food sharing of coordinates.
InformationChannel: Shared marks among active foragers, separate task activation
EvidenceLocators: B2-P08 pp. 62–68, Results, Figs. 1–5, Tables 1–2 | B2-P09 pp. 562–566, Results and discussion, Fig. 1, Tables 1–3 | B2-P11 pp. 191–194, Results, Figs. 1–3 and A1 | B2-P12 Accepted manuscript pp. 12–16, Experiments 1 and 0, Figs. 1, 2 and 4 | B2-P12-C Accepted manuscript pp. 13–14, Experiment 2 results, Fig. 3 | B2-P15 pp. 753–756, Results, Eq. 1–5, Fig. 1, Tables I–II
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Scout return, nestmate exit, relay and time-resolved colony feeder occupancy
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Mass foraging in the tested colonies includes regulated leaving and mark reinforcement. Controlled worker contact did not convey the next turn in P12. The congener control is separate.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A surface field acts on workers already in the decision loop. There is no modeled effect of scout marks on a nestmate becoming a forager, no pre-feeder relay and no route-aware group feedback test matched to these papers.

CodeElement: Trail, discovery and trip observables
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Report visited tiles, undirected edge traversals, counted first discovery, active trail cells, current units and deposited-minus-current units. Discovery is a recorded cue and differs from a collection.
InformationChannel: Read-only accounting and behavioral observation labels
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint for software counters
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Counters summarize committed movement, food cues and artificial field state.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Visited edges, candidate-source discovery, a signal-bearing step and mass delivered answer different questions. Deposited minus live units includes cutoff losses and is not chemical evaporation measured in nature.

CodeElement: Unexamined cell → Local cue / no cue
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Bounded BFS samples a unique walkable reachable cell | Nonempty source in local index. Continuous mode requires clear food segment | Append resource, cell, distance and first direction to LocalObservation
EvidenceLocators: B2-F04 pp. 76–78, §§3.1–3.2, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B2-F08 pp. 117–121, Results and interpretation, Figs. 1–4, Table 1
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Antennal contacts and feeding after contact at an offered droplet
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Experimental intake can follow sensory contact, with acceptance dependent on stimulus.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A cue or no cue is an exact nonempty reachable-cell result. Virtual samples and solid clearance do not model contact latency or odor detection through air.

CodeElement: Candidate edge → Legal cue / excluded
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Inspect adjacent cardinal cell | Open cell, current swept clearance. Trail key uses own colony only | Set trail cue from decayed field or zero
EvidenceLocators: B2-P10 p. 796, species-specific and stereochemical tests, Scheme 1 and Fig. 1, Tables 1–2 | B2-P15 pp. 753–756, Results, Eq. 1–5, Fig. 1, Tables I–II | B2-P16 pp. 1618–1622, Results and model fit, Figs. 2, 4 and 6, Table 1 and Online Appendix B Tables B1–B3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Antenna activity, response on foreign donor paper and extract-based branch choices
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Species can detect and choose some marked paper even without same-colony identity.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Eligibility uses cell passability plus an exact own-colony key and deterministic decay. No measured detection range or cue mixing supports that guard.

CodeElement: Unenrolled → Enabled with Wake
CurrentRuleOrGuard: External request or physiological program entry | Worker, live adult, surface, unloaded and positive capacity. Validate home and pending conflicts | Initialize trace and seeded heading. First wake at legal zero time or after decision_delay
InformationChannel: Eligibility, private trace and event initialization
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No comparable event clock or registration endpoint
SupportedBiologicalClaim: The transition creates an owned software wake for an eligible actor.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The experimental departures in FOR-01 do not imply a zero-time or 1 ms biological trigger.

CodeElement: Explore / FollowTrail / FollowMemory / Collect / Return / Rest → Deliver
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Loaded and current cell equals recorded home | Connector can replace action with physical return before delivery | Propose DeliverFood
EvidenceLocators: B2-P09 pp. 562–566, Results and discussion, Fig. 1, Tables 1–3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Scouts returning and unloading after contact with sucrose
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Loaded scouts bring food back and transfer it in the nest.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Cargo at a known cell immediately proposes one delivery or a connector leg. The paper does not measure exact depot contact or bulk transfer of a full load.

CodeElement: Explore / FollowTrail / FollowMemory / Return → Return / Rest
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Away from home and loaded, already Return, path at capacity or moves at cap | Previous trace edge must be among legal local steps. Default Rest if unavailable | Propose trace-reversal Move or idle action
EvidenceLocators: B2-F02 pp. 289–296, rotation and light interventions, Figs. 12–14, Tables II–IV | B2-F05 pp. 503–504, §3.1, Fig. 1, Tables 1–2
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Return-track variation and additional drinking on return
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Homeward movement can use directional cues and can be interrupted by intake.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The chosen predecessor is exact and any cargo forces return before local food. Missing predecessor leads to a Rest action. No equivalent move or trace cap was measured.

CodeElement: Searching with local food → Explore / Collect
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Nearest reachable cue selected. Equal distances uniformly drawn | Same cell -> Collect. Otherwise cue's recorded first step -> Explore with LocalFood reason | Propose physical move or collection. Exact food coordinates are consulted only for a selected local cue in continuous mode
InformationChannel: Nearest exact local cue and tie draw
EvidenceLocators: B2-F04 pp. 76–78, §§3.1–3.2, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B2-F08 pp. 117–121, Results and interpretation, Figs. 1–4, Table 1 | B2-P15 pp. 753–756, Results, Eq. 1–5, Fig. 1, Tables I–II
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Post-contact food acceptance and sugar-dependent colony exploitation
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Food identity and quality can affect observed foraging outcomes.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The local-first ranking is defined by graph cells, not comparative odor or taste. Uniform ties address a software bias, with no experiment isolating this guard.

CodeElement: No local food with memory → FollowMemory / fall through
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Current cell on unexpired learned path and another step exists | Next remembered step must be legal. Expire if elapsed strictly greater than lifetime | Propose remembered move or request forgetting on expiry, blocked next edge or endpoint
EvidenceLocators: B2-F06 pp. 144–146, Results, experiments 1–5, Figs. 1–4 | B2-F07 pp. 190–193, Results, Figs. 1–4 and 6, Appendix Tables A1–A2 pp. 195–196 | B2-P03 Results, Decision making and Pheromone deposition, Figs. 1–3, S1 Table | B2-P07 pp. 264–266, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Experienced route accuracy and context dependence, including negative learning result
SupportedBiologicalClaim: A learned route can be preferred over a conflicting cue but accuracy remains imperfect.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: No probabilistic memory retrieval, fixed five-minute expiry or forgetting on one blocked edge is supported. No trial isolates this exact ordered guard.

CodeElement: No higher-priority decision → Explore / FollowTrail / Rest
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Weighted draw among allowed steps after predecessor filter | No legal step returns Rest. FollowTrail label uses visible signal on selected edge | Queue Move or idle action under resolve_wakes
EvidenceLocators: B2-F01 PDF pp. 3–6, Effect of inclination and extended walker analysis, Figs. 1–5, Table 1 | B2-F03 PDF pp. 6–10, Results, Figs. 1–4 and S1.1–S1.12, Tables S1.1–S1.3 | B2-P01 pp. 772–774, Results and discussion, Figs. 1–3 | B2-P04 PDF pp. 4–6, Results, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Turning kernel and first fork choice with geometry and trail
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Turning structure, heading and cues can alter choices at these assays.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The underlying continuous angle and conditional hazards are not reproduced by four choices, categorical exclusion or exact constant weights.

CodeElement: Source stock → Carried / no transfer
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Committed CollectFood attempt | Contact, available mass, capacity minus soil and loaded clearance. Otherwise reject | Proportional integer mass allocation, Success/Partial and FoodCollected
EvidenceLocators: B2-F04 pp. 76–78, §§3.1–3.2, Figs. 1–3, Tables 1–2 | B2-F05 pp. 503–504, §3.1, Fig. 1, Tables 1–2 | B2-F08 pp. 117–121, Results and interpretation, Figs. 1–4, Table 1
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Drinking accepted per contact, elapsed seconds and ingested volume
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Contact may lead to uptake that depends on food and feeding state.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A capacity- and stock-limited mass commit is deterministic once eligible. It models neither liquid ingestion kinetics nor a crop target. Capacity fairness is engineering.

CodeElement: Collect → Return
CurrentRuleOrGuard: FoodCollected fact from the owned action | Memory-enabled flag gates copy of path. Partial successful collection also learns | Set last resource, collection/revisit counters and learned time
EvidenceLocators: B2-F06 pp. 144–146, Results, experiments 1–5, Figs. 1–4 | B2-F07 pp. 190–193, Results, Figs. 1–4 and 6, Appendix Tables A1–A2 pp. 195–196
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Branch choice on later visits after rewarded experience
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Success at a food source is associated with route learning.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: The overwrite snapshots the whole current path even for a partial collection. First-trip memory in the paper is imperfect, and the return guard bypasses uncertainty.

CodeElement: Deliver → Explore / retry after rejection
CurrentRuleOrGuard: DeliverFood resolved at depot contact | Reachable actual nest, same legacy tile where applicable, nonempty cargo | Move full cargo to nest stock. After_action resets mode/trip on success
EvidenceLocators: B2-P09 pp. 562–566, Results and discussion, Fig. 1, Tables 1–3
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Unloading scout and within-nest contact timing
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Returning scouts unload food and interact with nestmates.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Full mass deposited in nest stock in one fact differs from transfer to recipient crops. The exact contact threshold and next wake are not measured.

CodeElement: Unloaded surface trip → Home cell / connector returning
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Actual move reaches home cell with no food | Set connector returning only if an actual multi-point connector exists | Reset trip count and mode. Schedule next wake to traverse connector if present
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No matched empty-return cursor experiment
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Arriving at a tile can start a physically checked connector leg.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Resetting trip counts and traversing the saved path are not measured nest-recognition dynamics.

CodeElement: Scheduled Move → Moved / ActionRejected
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Action resolution after issued duration | Bounds, swept clearance, valid legacy adjacency and speed. Reject stale position earlier | Update real coordinates, revision and contact indexes on success
EvidenceLocators: B2-F01 PDF pp. 3–6, Effect of inclination and extended walker analysis, Figs. 1–5, Table 1 | B2-F09 pp. 538–540, §§3.1–3.3, Figs. 1–3 | B2-P04 PDF pp. 4–6, Results, Figs. 1–5
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: Continuous time series of realized unloaded motion
SupportedBiologicalClaim: Real trajectory speeds and headings vary with assay context.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Geometry and elapsed-limit checks determine whether a proposed endpoint commits. No source calibrates the static speed cap, adjacency rejection or atomic jump in event representation.

CodeElement: Outbound or returning cursor → Move / Rest / Deliver
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Active connector leg or loaded return at depot | Test next waypoint segment with actual loaded or unloaded half-extent | Propose valid waypoint movement. At cursor zero returning, deliver if loaded or Rest if empty
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No matched worker geometry search experiment
SupportedBiologicalClaim: A segment test checks the proposed path using body extent.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Cursor order and Rest on blockage do not establish navigation knowledge or animal rest.

CodeElement: Prior connector cursor → Next connector cursor
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Committed Moved fact exactly at expected waypoint | No cursor increment on failed movement. Empty arrival at depot clears returning | Update saved cursor and connector evidence
InformationChannel: Connector cursor updated by committed movement
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint
SupportedBiologicalClaim: The cursor moves only after the matching position commits.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: Exact waypoint equality and stored return cursor preserve reproducibility.

CodeElement: Owned action or active schedule → Next Wake / disabled
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Completed/rejected action or stop | Death/explicit program stop removes pending work. Rejection does not remove ownership | Schedule after decision_delay or disable wake/action
MeasuredEndpointAndUnit: No biological endpoint
SupportedBiologicalClaim: The queue obeys decision ownership across rejection, stopping and death.
UnsupportedImplementationOrGap: A same-boundary ordering or replay invariant does not estimate individual temporal response.

CodeElement: Existing decayed stock or empty → Capped deposit
CurrentRuleOrGuard: Successful cross-tile movement with prior food cargo and trails enabled | Connector and same-tile branches bypass this deposition. Host sparse limit checked | Commit min(cap, current + increment). Record added units
EvidenceLocators: B2-P05 PDF pp. 4–6, §§3.1–3.3, Figs. 2–3 | B2-P06 pp. 371–373, Results, Figs. 1–3, Table 1 | B2-P08 pp. 62–68, Results, Figs. 1–5, Tables 1–2 | B2-P09 pp. 562–566, Results and discussion, Fig. 1, Tables 1–3 | B2-P10 p. 796, species-specific and stereochemical tests, Scheme 1 and Fig. 1, Tables 1–2 | B2-P15 pp. 753–756, Results, Eq. 1–5, Fig. 1, Tables I–II
